newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: OUB says no idea how share issue leaked.
newsitem.headline: OUB says no idea how share issue leaked.

text.p: The president and chief executive officer of Singapore's Overseas Union Bank Ltd (OUB), Peter Seah, said on Friday it did not know how news of his bank's rights share issue had leaked onto the stock market.

Told by reporters at the group's financial results news conference that Reuters had carried accurate details of the one-for-five rights issue at around 0500 GMT on Friday, three hours before the bank's official announcement of the issue, Seah expressed surprise.
But he said he was not overly worried, since the bank's shares had been suspended on Friday ahead of its results.
"The share was already suspended. Perhaps people with access to the information may not have kept quiet," he said. "A lot of people have to be involved in a share issue."
Reuters earlier quoted dealers correctly reporting that the rights issue would be priced at Singapore $4.00 per share for local shares and at S$6.91 for the foreign shares.
